findings.source_quote: τούτοις οὖν ἐστὶ μετάνοια, ἐὰν ταχὺ μετανοήσωσι καὶ μὴ ἐπιμείνωσι ταῖς ἡδοναῖς αὐτῶν·
findings.english_quote: These still have an opportunity to repent if they repent quickly and do not persist in their pleasures.
findings.issue: Paragraph 5 introduces explicit continuative emphasis with “still,” although the selected clause lacks ἔτι. Paragraph 3 expressly includes ἔτι, so using “still” in both conceals an observable source distinction. Note d acknowledges the difference but gives the Michigan reading as an alternative identical to the main English. Disclosure does not preserve the selected wording distinction when the main text incorporates the variant’s explicit emphasis.
findings.suggested_revision: For fresh review, consider: “So these have an opportunity to repent if they repent quickly and do not persist in their pleasures.” Retain paragraph 3’s “still.” Adjust note d to distinguish the selected clause from the reported Michigan alternative containing “still,” without describing that alternative as already incorporated into the main text.

findings.source_quote: τούτοις οὖν ἐστὶ μετάνοια, ἐὰν ταχὺ μετανοήσωσι καὶ μὴ ἐπιμείνωσι ταῖς ἡδοναῖς αὐτῶν·
findings.english_quote: These still have an opportunity to repent if they repent quickly and do not keep pursuing their pleasures.
findings.issue: Against the Greek independently, paragraph 5 adds “still” where the selected clause has no ἔτι, while paragraph 3 does have that explicit wording. Simplification therefore removes a source distinction rather than merely shortening syntax. Note d acknowledges the reported Michigan addition, but its alternative is identical to the main rendering.
findings.suggested_revision: For fresh review, consider: “So these have an opportunity to repent if they repent quickly and do not keep pursuing their pleasures.” Keep “still” in paragraph 3, and revise note d so the reported Michigan wording remains a distinguishable alternative.

summary: Both editions cover the selected clauses and preserve the rod groups, negations, conditional repentance, and death warnings. The working proportions and reported Athos alternative are appropriately distinguished. A small revision is needed in paragraph 5 to preserve the selected source’s distinction from paragraph 3 and from the reported Michigan wording. Proposed replacements require fresh review. This assessment concerns the supplied Greek and bounded project reports, not authentication of unseen manuscripts or exhaustive collation.
